title: Finite mixed-unit normalization of the realized scalar comparison
statement: Let $K_0$ be a field and $\ell$ a prime invertible in $K_0$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism between finite-type $K_0$-schemes, fix a compactification $c$, and let $E,L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra embedding $\iota:E\to L$. Equip $X,Y$ with the residue-field units induced by the given base-field unit [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the fixed integral functors $F_E,F_L$ [def-weil-compact-support-finite-action] and completed scalar extensions $T^W$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For any integral natural isomorphism $b:F_ET^Y\simeq T^XF_L$ whose ambient components are $T^Y(\rho_E)\,\operatorname{coefficientExchange}(\operatorname{systemCompactScalar})\,\rho_L^{-1}$ [def-weil-system-operation-exchange-realization], the predicate SfCompactSupportIntegralBetaSpec [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action] holds: at every input and quotient level the specified mixed output unit gives the Hom bijection for all derived targets, and reduction of $b$ followed by the fixed target reduction is exactly its uniquely determined finite compact-support mate. This asserts only normalization of a given comparison, not existence or invertibility of that comparison.

source.place: Compact-support and final paragraphs; normalized scalar isomorphisms proof steps 1, 5

proof.text: Fix K and n. Apply the generic completed mixed-unit Hom bijection at Y to the integral compact-support value F_E K. Precomposition by the inverse specified reduction isomorphism r_E is the Iso.homCongr equivalence. Compose these two bijections: by associativity this is exactly the output-unit function in SfCompactSupportIntegralBetaSpec, for every unbounded target.

Choose that proof hN of bijectivity. By injectivity of Equiv.ofBijective, equality with sfCompactSupportFiniteMate reduces to its specified transpose. Replace the ambient component of b by the hypothesis hb, apply the realized-scalar transpose equation, and cancel r_E inverse followed by r_E. This proves the precise beta specification without changing any comparison data.

theorem sfCompactSupportFiniteScalarMateNormalization
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ y : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField y)]
    (E L : Type u) [Field E] [Field L]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [Algebra (Padic l) L]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) L]
    (ι : E →ₐ[Padic l] L)
    (b : sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l K₀ hl c E ⋙
        sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l
          (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime)) E L ι Y ≅
      sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l
          (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime)) E L ι X ⋙
        sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l K₀ hl c L)
    (hb : ∀ K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X,
      (b.hom.app K).hom = (integralScalarExtension l E L ι Y).map
          ((FrobeniusExchange.compactRealization l E K₀ hl f c).hom.app K) ≫
        (FrobeniusExchange.coefficientExchange l E L ι
          (FrobeniusExchange.systemDerivedOpen l E c.i ⋙ FrobeniusExchange.systemDirect l E c.g)
          (FrobeniusExchange.systemDerivedOpen l L c.i ⋙ FrobeniusExchange.systemDirect l L c.g)
          (FrobeniusExchange.systemCompactScalar l E L ι c)).app K ≫
        (FrobeniusExchange.compactRealization l L K₀ hl f c).inv.app
          ((sfConstructibleIntegralScalarExtension 0 l
            (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime)) E L ι X).obj K)) :
    SfCompactSupportIntegralBetaSpec l K₀ hl c E L ι b
